findings.title: collectHookFeesByHook lacks nonReentrant modifier — reentrancy window during queued fee execution
findings.description: collectHookFeesByHook (ModuleFeeCollection.sol:72) is the ONLY external state-changing function without nonReentrant modifier. During _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers (AMMModule.sol:3183), _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) clears ALL custom flags while preserving ENTERED bit. If the fee token is ERC-777 or similar callback token, the recipient receives a callback where SWAP_GUARD_FLAG is cleared. collectHookFeesByHook then falls through to direct _transferHookFeesByHook. However, CEI pattern in _transferHookFeesByHook (decrement tokensOwed BEFORE transfer) prevents double-spending. Reentrant call can only collect remaining owed amount.
findings.impact: No value extraction possible. CEI pattern is correctly implemented. The structural concern is that the function relies on storage-level CEI rather than reentrancy guards for safety.
attack_sequence: 2. Hook calls collectHookFeesByHook during a swap → gets queued
6. Direct transfer path entered (no flags set)
7. Second _transferHookFeesByHook can only claim REMAINING owed balance
8. No double-spend: total claimed <= total owed
findings.root_cause: Missing nonReentrant modifier on collectHookFeesByHook combined with flag clearing in _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers
findings.why_below_threshold: CEI pattern prevents value extraction. No attacker profit, no material victim harm, no protocol bricking. Structural defense-in-depth concern only.

findings.title: validateHandlerOrder does not check sqrtPriceX96==0 overflow — bounds bypass for max-only pricing
findings.description: When SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96 overflows uint160, it returns 0. In validateHandlerOrder (line 221), the check 'sqrtPriceX96 > bounds.maxSqrtPriceX96' evaluates to false when sqrtPriceX96=0, allowing orders at prices exceeding the intended maximum. The AMM's _validatePricingBounds (line 847-849) correctly checks for sqrtPriceX96==0 but validateHandlerOrder does not. This is already documented as CP-003 in confirmed-patterns.md.
findings.impact: Handler orders (CLOB/Permit) can bypass max-only pricing bounds set by token admins. However, both maker and taker explicitly consent to the specific amounts in the order, limiting real-world impact.
attack_sequence: 1. Token admin sets pricing bounds: min=0 (unset), max=X
2. Attacker crafts handler order with extreme amount ratio
5. Order executes at price above intended maximum
findings.root_cause: Missing sqrtPriceX96==0 check in validateHandlerOrder, inconsistent with _validatePricingBounds
findings.why_below_threshold: Already known (CP-003). Both order participants consent to amounts. Low economic impact.
